newsitem.title: SPAIN: Retevision says no decision yet on bid.
newsitem.headline: Retevision says no decision yet on bid.

text.p: Spain's second telephone operator Retevision said on Thursday it had still not set a date to announce the winning bidder in its privatisation.
"The process of evaluating the offers is continuing and there is still no date fixed to announce the results," a spokesman at Retevision said.
The government is selling a 70 percent stake in state broadcaster Retevision along with the licence to compete in basic services with Telefonica de Espana.

After the presentation of offers on June 9, Spain's Development Minister Rafael Arias-Salgado said the winning bid could be announced at the end of June or the beginning of July. conditions of the auction, a period of two months had been allotted to the evaluation of bids.

The competition is now between two consortiums: a group including Spanish electricity firm Endesa and Italy's Stet which have offered 180 billion pesetas for the stake; and the Opera group comprising Spanish bank BCH, France Telecom and U.S. operator Sprint which have presented an offer of 130 billion pesetas.
While Opera has been outbid financially, it said it could still win on other factors such as infrastructure and the future benefits for the Spanish economy.
